field_diff.before: Models economic fluctuations driven by technology shocks. Nobel Prize work by Kydland & Prescott. DOI: 10.2307/1913386
field_diff.after: Illustrative fixed-saving discrete growth experiment with AR(1) log technology. It is not a solution or replication of the optimizing Kydland-Prescott or Dynare RBC equilibrium. The one-period difference contract is explicit: Euler step exactly 1 is required. Log technology satisfies log(A_next/A_ss)=rho*log(A/A_ss)+epsilon, implemented as the next level minus the current level; rho .95 is persistence rather than a positive continuous growth coefficient. Investment, current consumption, wages and return use current Production instead of accumulated output. The original stock IDs, all flows, connectors and geometry are preserved; the two accumulation stocks are explicitly named Cumulative Output and Cumulative Consumption, while Output and Consumption remain visible as current-rate outputs. Existing alpha .36, delta .025, fixed labor 100, savings .2 and sinusoidal epsilon are retained. No shock calibration or optimal savings/labor policy is claimed.
Technology_SS * EXP(Rho * LN(Technology / Technology_SS) + Epsilon) - Technology

field_diff.before: A model of electrical grid frequency stability, capturing the balance between generation and demand, inertia from rotating machines, and frequency response mechanisms. Critical for renewable integration. Reference: IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics. Source: https://www.irena.org/
field_diff.after: Illustrative grid-frequency experiment with physically consistent rotating-energy balance. Power is MW, time seconds, frequency Hz and kinetic energy MW s. Initial stored energy is derived from the existing System Inertia (5 s) times Base Generation (1000 MW), rather than an independent inconsistent 100. The net Inertial Response is demand minus generation, allowing both kinetic discharge and recharge. Frequency Change follows the exact nonlinear swing-energy identity df/dt=(Pgen-Pload)*f/(2E), retaining E/(f/f0)^2=5000 MW s. Adaptive Radau preserves the kinetic invariant to relative error below 2e-11 over the full 60 s, keeps the original output step .01, and permits half/quarter output refinements within the work budget. All original elements, geometry, forcing, droop and reserve paths remain. Governor/droop/reserve dynamics are illustrative local assumptions; this is not a reproduction of the NREL virtual-synchronous-generator network.
